title: An explicit normalized-j test family
quote: schéma en courbes elliptiques … invariant … j
context: Adds an explicit test to CT54/003,005 and CT44/008’s abelian realization framework; no matching family formula in CT
body: On \(U=\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf C}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\), take \(E_t:y^2=x^3-3t(t-1)^{-1}x-2t(t-1)^{-1}\). Direct calculation gives \(\Delta=1728t^2/(t-1)^3\) and \(j_{\mathrm{classical}}=1728t\), so this is a smooth family realizing the normalized coordinate t. Confidence: high, because the discriminant is invertible on U and the j-formula is an exact computation; this verifies a test construction, not the conjectural reconstruction of arbitrary places.

title: Numerical semisimplicity does not identify the cohomological category
context: Differs from CT16/049’s conditional cohomological semisimplicity programme and CN S15; adds a distinction needed for the automorphism group on 15/213 and the cancelled normalized-group claim on 18/012
body: Jannsen (1992, Theorem 1) proves semisimplicity for numerical motives with characteristic-zero coefficients, without identifying numerical and homological equivalence. Applying that theorem to the cohomological category intended in CT16/049 therefore requires a further comparison, including the chosen realization. Semisimplicity of a category, pro-reductivity of its tensor group and semisimplicity of the normalized algebraic group in the cancelled 18/012 draft are three distinct assertions.

title: The normalized group does not determine the central Tate data
context: Adds a normalized-period application to CT16/003–004,017’s grading and uniqueness discussions; differs from the operator-ring setting and bears directly on the separate GL₂ uniqueness entry in context/notes/RESULTS_STATE.md
ledger: LM1 A.8 [Refuted, the return’s claim]; MPL_14_002-044 B04 [first-pass lead]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]
body: The cancelled draft passes from the normalized group to G by adjoining the homotheties, so its central Tate data must be retained. LM1 A.8 already records a refutation of unqualified GL₂ uniqueness from fixed SL₂ data; the present note cites that status without rederiving the return. The new witness therefore calls for the determinant or Tate character and its normalization to be specified before upgrading normalized group generation to a statement about the full group.

title: The integral Hodge structure separates points in the test family
quote: foncteur dans les structures de Hodge ?; d’invariant l’indéterminée \(j\)
context: Adds an explicit integral test to CT54/003,005 and CT44/008’s abelian realization framework; no chosen-point injectivity argument of this form was located in the supplied context
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 M24a [first-pass lead]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; this is a conditional test, not a status change]
body: For an elliptic curve, recover its analytic torus as \(E(\mathbf C)\simeq(F^1H^1(E,\mathbf C))^\vee/\iota H_1(E,\mathbf Z)\), where \(\iota(\gamma)(\omega)=\int_\gamma\omega\); the integral Hodge structure determines this construction (Milne, 2005/2017, Theorem 6.8). An integral Hodge isomorphism therefore induces a holomorphic group isomorphism of the elliptic curves, so for the family X01 it implies \(1728t_1=1728t_2\) and hence \(t_1=t_2\). Confidence: high, because the period embedding of the actual lattice, together with the exact j-calculation, gives the implication without an additional chosen polarization. Replacing the integral lattice by rational cohomology retains only the isogeny class, so this proof does not establish equality of j in that variant (Milne, 2005/2017, Corollary 6.9).

title: A conditional separation of chosen complex embeddings
quote: Attention, il faut parler des pl. complexes
context: Adds an objectwise integral criterion to CT54/003,005 and the abelian comparisons in CT44/008–009; the supplied materials do not state this chosen-embedding separation argument
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 M24a and §3 [first-pass leads]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; restricted injectivity evidence only]
body: Let \(\sigma,\tau:k\hookrightarrow\mathbf C\) be chosen field embeddings, and suppose their Betti–Hodge realizations are isomorphic on an integral category containing \(h^1(E_a)\) for every \(a\in k\setminus\{0,1\}\), with the X01 family defined over k. Applying X02 objectwise gives \(1728\sigma(a)=1728\tau(a)\) for every such a, hence \(\sigma=\tau\), since embeddings also fix 0 and 1. Confidence: high for this conditional implication, because it uses only the reconstructed elliptic curves and the explicit invariant; even objectwise integral Hodge isomorphisms suffice. The hypotheses require preservation of the integral lattice and ordinary Hodge type over the identity of \(\mathbf C\); they do not settle the rational-functor variant, the essential image, or a formulation that identifies conjugate Hodge structures.
